say: Good morning, Measure Masters! Today we measure how long, how heavy, how much water and how much time.
Some puzzles today have no ruler, no scale with numbers and no marks on the jugs. We will use our heads: notice it, test it, explain why.
I will show you something. Write the unit you would use to measure it on your whiteboard: m, cm, kg, g, ℓ or minutes. Show me on three.
Be ready to say why. Why not grams for a bag of rice?
Look at your balance. A glue stick goes in one cup. How many 20¢ coins will balance it? Write your guess before you test.
stuck: Stuck: check the hanger is level with both cups empty before you start.
Coins keep sliding: put them in the cup one at a time and stop when the hanger is level.
Finished early: find something that balances exactly the same number of coins as your glue stick.

say: “A watermelon balances 3 pineapples. One pineapple balances a 2 kg weight. The scale is level, so both sides are equally heavy. I can swap each pineapple for 2 kg: 2, 4, 6. The watermelon is 6 kg.”

“Now the watermelon balances one pineapple and 4 bags of sugar. The watermelon is 6 kg and the pineapple is 2 kg, so the bags must be the rest: 6 − 2 = 4 kg. 4 bags make 4 kg, so each bag is 1 kg. I check: 2 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 6 ✓.”

“A jug puzzle: a 4 ℓ jug and a 9 ℓ jug, and I want exactly 1 ℓ. I fill the 9 ℓ jug. I pour into the 4 ℓ jug until it is full: 9 − 4 = 5 left. I empty the 4 ℓ jug and pour again: 5 − 4 = 1. I write every pour in a table so I can check it.”

do: Ask: “The scale is level. What does that tell you?”
Ask: “What can you swap the melon for?”
Ask: “How much is in each jug now? Show me in your table.”
stuck: Hint 1: “Find the thing you know first. Which scale has a number on it?”
Hint 2: “Swap: put what balances it on the scale instead.”
Hint 3: “For jugs, write the two amounts after every pour.”

do: Ask: “The scale is level. What does that tell you?”
Ask: “What can you swap the melon for?”
Ask: “How much is in each jug now? Show me in your table.”
stuck: Hint 1: “Find the thing you know first. Which scale has a number on it?”
Hint 2: “Swap: put what balances it on the scale instead.”
Hint 3: “For jugs, write the two amounts after every pour.”

say: “How did swapping help you with the balance puzzles?”
ask: “How did swapping help you with the balance puzzles?”

A level balance means the two sides weigh the same, so the melon can be swapped for 2 apples (or 400 g) and the scale stays level. (If a pair finishes early: a table shows how much is in each jug after every pour, so we can check every step and find our way back.)

say: “You were real Measure Masters today. You swapped things on a balance, you found exact amounts with no marks on the jugs, and you counted time across the hour.”
Next lesson is Puzzle Day: bring your best thinking!

p2l9-title.note: Objective: Solve balance-scale puzzles in g and kg by swapping things that balance; solve pouring puzzles with litre jugs by keeping a table of every pour; join and cut lengths in m and cm (overlaps, pieces and cuts); tell the time to 5 minutes with am and pm and find start times, end times and how long, also across the hour. Materials: A coat hanger, two paper cups, string, a glue stick, a spoon and about 20 20¢ coins (a home-made balance; backup: a ruler balanced on a pencil); for the jug puzzles two cups or bottles of different size (about 3 and 5 units), a jug of dry rice or sand (or water), and tape marking 3 and 5 units; a cardboard clock with hands; mini whiteboards. Online: Children build the coat-hanger balance before the lesson and describe it aloud (nothing is held up to the camera). No coat-hanger balance at home? Balance a ruler on a pencil on camera and let pairs share one view. Share the slide balances, jugs and clocks and annotate on screen. Each child needs a cardboard or paper-plate clock. For the pouring puzzles use dry rice or sand rather than water when online, and let children act out each pour with the two containers. Time plan: opening 0 to 1.5, sneak-peek puzzles 1.5 to 6, warm-up 6 to 10.5, explore 10.5 to 23.5, mini-lesson 23.5 to 34, brain break 34 to 37, worksheet page 1 37 to 51, check together, page 1 51 to 53.5, short teaching 53.5 to 58, worksheet page 2 58 to 69.5, check together, page 2 69.5 to 72, flex (spare time) 72 to 76.5, talk time 76.5 to 81.5, exit ticket 81.5 to 86.5, looking back 86.5 to 88.5, closing and stamps 88.5 to 90. The Think harder and Go further slides are optional, if you finish early (no clock time). Kit ready at minute 0: ask families to put every item on the desk before the lesson starts (a 30-second check at the start). SPINE: Today's tool is Make a table. Put what you know in rows and columns. Look for where you use it. Point at the card on page 1 of the workbook.

p2l9-tool.note: SPINE: Show for about 20 seconds, inside the opening. Today's tool is Make a table. Put what you know in rows and columns. Look for where you use it. Point at the card on page 1 of the workbook.

p2l9-precheck.note: Minutes 1.5 to 6. Sneak-peek puzzles: two puzzles on the key idea of today, which the children have NOT learnt yet. Say out loud (about 28 words): "Two sneak-peek puzzles on ideas we have not learnt yet. Guessing is welcome, so is I do not know. Nobody is marked. Say your answer together on three." Question 1 is an access question: any child can try it with objects, a drawing or counting, so everyone has a first win (about 45 seconds). Question 2 is the thinking question (about 90 seconds). Then about 2 minutes for the answers slide and the move on. Answers are PRIVATE: each child writes on their own paper and says the answer together on three; nothing is held up to the camera. Do not raise whiteboards together, do not read answers out, do not name children. Q1 answer: 2 ℓ (5 - 3 = 2). Listen for: One pour is enough. This is a first win for everyone and previews the pour table. Q2 answer: 6 plums (3 + 3). Listen for: Listen for swapping: the melon can be swapped for 2 apples, and each apple for 3 plums. Drawing the scale is a good method. At the end click to show the answers as "one way to think about it", without saying who had what. Ask only for volunteers: "Would anyone like to tell us how they started?" Invite the WHOLE group at once, never one child: "When you have finished Start here, you can choose Think harder, Go further or the Investigation." Never announce who is on which page. Pairs are not split unless both children agree. Children can move either way at any time. Everyone joins explore, the mini-lesson, the check-together slides and talk time.

p2l9-warm1.note: Minutes 6 to 8.5. Which unit? Point to one card at a time. Children write the unit on whiteboards and say it together on three. Then click to show the unit (clicks reveal door, rice, brushing teeth in order: three prompts only; pencil, strawberry and bucket are spare). Answers: door m (about 2 m), pencil cm, bag of rice kg, strawberry g, bucket of water ℓ, brushing teeth minutes (about 2 minutes). Ask "Why not grams for the rice?" (the number would be very big; kilograms are the bigger unit) and "Why not metres for the pencil?" (a pencil is much shorter than 1 m). Quick finisher: "Name something you would measure in litres at home." (a bottle of water, a pot of soup, a fish tank). Watch for children who mix up length and mass: "Is a heavy thing always long?" A game of about 2.5 minutes: stop it on the clock even if the game is not finished.

p2l9-warm2.note: Minutes 8.5 to 10.5. Read each question aloud, give thinking time, take answers, then click to show. Ask "How do you know?" each time. Answers: 1) 75 cm (30 + 40 = 70, 5 more). 2) 3 ℓ (count on from 2 to 5). Spare questions in the guide table: the minute hand on 6 is 30 minutes past; lunch at 12:30 is pm (draw a day line from midnight to midnight and mark noon); 2 bags of 5 kg are 10 kg. Ask quick questions 1 and 3 only (about 2 minutes): children answer by thumbs, hands, not by naming a child. The other questions are spare.

p2l9-explore1.note: Minutes 10.5 to 19.5. The coat-hanger balance is hung and tested level BEFORE the lesson (kit message, then a 30-second check at minute 0). Only the glue stick is tested in class (the spoon is a take-home). Pair work is 5.5 minutes. Pairs use their coat-hanger balance. Online: children describe their balance aloud; if a child has none, they balance two objects in their hands and guess which is heavier, then check on a kitchen scale with an adult. Say: "Before you add any coins, write your guess." Walk round and ask: "How do you know it is level?" "What happens if you add one more coin?" Do not teach the swapping idea yet: let children notice that the number of coins tells us how heavy the object is. Go further (a second what-if, so nobody waits) is the box at the foot of this slide; the question is also posted in the chat when the pairs go to their breakout rooms. It is for ANY child who finishes the explore task or wants more: say it to the whole group as a choice, never as a prize, and never name who tries it. Pairs stay together unless both children agree to split. Answer: 24 coins (3 x 8). 6 erasers (24 / 4). Take it at the debrief only if a pair offers it.

p2l9-explore2.note: Minutes 19.5 to 23.5. Let pairs keep testing, then gather to answer these one at a time. What we want them to notice: when the balance is level, the two sides are equally heavy, so the coins tell us how heavy the object is in "coins". Answers: 1) Open: compare with other pairs. 2) The glue stick: it needs more of the same coin to balance. 3) Erasers and coins are different units (an eraser is not as heavy as a coin), so the numbers are different. To compare, use the same unit. Follow-up: "If the glue stick balances 8 coins and 2 glue sticks are on one side, how many coins balance them?" (16). Keep it moving (about 4 minutes in all): ask "how do you know?" on question 2 only; about 15 seconds of talk on the other questions.

p2l9-teach1.note: Minutes 23.5 to 25.5. Teach: the idea and why. Hold up the coat-hanger balance: "Level means both sides are equally heavy." Click 1: "1 pineapple balances 3 oranges. Each orange is 200 g. How heavy is the pineapple?" Let children guess first. Click 2: "If one orange is just as heavy as a 200 g weight, I can take the orange off and put the weight on instead. Is it still level?" (Yes.) Click 3 shows the weights. Click 4: count on in 200s: 200, 400, 600. Click 5: the why. Think-aloud: "The scale is level, so both sides are the same. I swap each orange for what it balances. The scale stays level, so the pineapple is 600 g." Common mistake: adding the two sides together (pineapple + oranges). Ask: "Does a level balance tell us the two sides are the same or that we add them?"

p2l9-we1.note: Minutes 25.5 to 29. Worked example. Ask first: "Which scale should we start with? Why?" (the one with a number). Before each click, ask the group to predict. Think-aloud: "A watermelon balances 3 pineapples. One pineapple balances a 2 kg weight. The scale is level, so both sides are equally heavy. I can swap each pineapple for 2 kg: 2, 4, 6. The watermelon is 6 kg. Now the watermelon balances one pineapple and 4 bags of sugar. The watermelon is 6 kg and the pineapple is 2 kg, so the bags must be the rest: 6 − 2 = 4 kg. 4 bags make 4 kg, so each bag is 1 kg. I check scale C: 2 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 6 ✓." Common mistake in step 3: adding 6 + 2. Point to scale C: "The watermelon is on one side, the pineapple and the bags are on the other. The bags are what is left after the pineapple."

p2l9-try1.note: Minutes 29 to 30.5. Write it, say the answer together on three, then click. a) 100, 200, 300, 400: 400 g. b) Two cups share 300 g equally: 150 + 150 = 300, so 150 g. (Item c, the box and the balls, is dropped: it is worksheet Q1c.)

p2l9-we2.note: Minutes 30.5 to 33. Worked example (a jug puzzle). Say the table from the SAY lines, do not read the long table on the slide aloud. Use two real cups if you have them. Read the rules on the right first. Click to reveal each row; before each click ask "What could we do next?" Think-aloud: "I want exactly 1 ℓ. I fill the 9 ℓ jug. I pour into the 4 ℓ jug until it is full: 9 − 4 = 5 left. I empty the 4 ℓ jug and pour again: 5 − 4 = 1. I write every pour in a table so I can check it, and so I can find my way back if I get lost." Stress: after each step write how much is in EACH jug. Common mistake: "pour half". We cannot pour half: there are no marks, so a pour only stops when one jug is full or the other is empty.

p2l9-key.note: Minutes 33 to 34. Say the key idea together. Common mistakes to watch for during the worksheet: (1) Balance puzzles: adding the masses on the two sides instead of using "both sides are the same". (2) Q1c: forgetting to take the apple away before sharing among the lemons. (3) Jug puzzles: writing "pour" without how much is in each jug, so the steps cannot be checked; or "pouring half". (4) Time: counting on past the hour as if there were 100 minutes in an hour (4:50 + 35 minutes written as 4:85 or 5:85).

p2l9-break.note: Minutes 34 to 37. Three minutes: two of movement, one for a drink of water. Online: children stay in view of the camera. Finish with a drink of water.

p2l9-ws1.note: Minutes 37 to 51. Walk around. Ask "Which scale has a number?" and "How much is in each jug now?" before giving any help. Q1c: the melon is 400 g and the apple is 200 g, so the 4 lemons share the other 200 g. Q2(b) (get exactly 1 ℓ) is marked ★ take-home on the page: children do it at home. If children want to act it out, cups marked "3" and "5" and water or rice help. Say once, to everyone: "After question 3 you may choose: carry on, or try Think harder." Never say who is on which page. Invite the WHOLE group at once, never one child: "When you have finished Start here, you can choose Think harder, Go further or the Investigation." Pairs are not split unless both children agree.

p2l9-ws1ans.note: Minutes 51 to 53.5. Click each answer after a pair explains theirs (answer lines only). Q2(b) is a take-home star: the answer stays here so children can mark it at home. Q1: scale 2: apple = 100 + 100 = 200 g. Scale 1: melon = 2 apples = 400 g. Scale 3: melon 400 g = apple 200 g + 4 lemons, so the lemons are 200 g and each lemon is 50 g (50 + 50 + 50 + 50 = 200). d) 400 g is 8 lots of 50 g; or: the apple is 4 lemons (scale 3 with scale 1), so the melon is 4 + 4 = 8 lemons. Q2a: (3 ℓ jug, 5 ℓ jug) fill 5: (0, 5); pour: (3, 2). Q2b: fill 3: (3, 0); pour: (0, 3); fill 3: (3, 3); pour until the 5 ℓ jug is full, only 2 ℓ fit: (1, 5).

p2l9-teachclock.note: Minutes 53.5 to 56. Teach before worksheet page 2 (Q5 clocks). Use the cardboard clocks. Step 1: "The short hand tells the hour. It has gone past 7 but not reached 8." Step 2: count round in 5s together, pointing at each number. Click the answer. Click the day line: "From midnight until noon is am (the morning). From noon until midnight is pm (afternoon and night)." Your turn: breakfast is in the morning, so 7:35 am. Ask: "What would you be doing at 7:35 pm?" Common mistake: reading the hour from the number the short hand is nearest (8) instead of the one it has passed (7).

p2l9-teachdur.note: Minutes 56 to 58. Teach before worksheet page 2 (Q5b and Q5c). Draw the time line on the board. Click the jumps, then step 1 and step 2. Think-aloud: "An hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so I cannot just add 45 + 35. I jump to the o’clock first: 2:45 to 3:00 is 15 minutes. I still need 35 − 15 = 20 minutes: 3:20 pm" Second example: "How long from 9:50 am to 11:05 am? I jump to the next o’clock: 10 minutes. Then whole hours: 10:00 to 11:00 is 1 hour. Then the minutes left: 5. Altogether 1 hour 15 minutes." Common mistakes: writing 2:80; counting 9:50 to 11:05 as 2 hours because the hour changes twice.

p2l9-ws2.note: Minutes 58 to 69.5. Children work alone. Note who needs a short catch-up. Q3 starts from empty jugs with the first two rows printed, so every child can begin. Q4(b) and Q5(c) are marked ★ take-home on the page: children do them at home. The trip across noon (Think harder 2) and the 20 m rope (Think harder 1) are on the Think harder page. Tutor rule at minute 58: if the clock is more than 2 minutes late, drop the last Core question of page 2 to take-home (children draw a star beside it). Never shorten talk time, the exit ticket, looking back or the closing. Questions marked with a star and the words take-home on the page are done at home; their answers are still on the check-together slide.

p2l9-ws2ans.note: Minutes 69.5 to 72. Click each answer after a child explains (answer lines only). Q4(b) and Q5(c) are take-home stars: the answers stay here so children can mark them at home. Q3 (3 ℓ jug, 5 ℓ jug): start (0, 0); fill 5 (0, 5); pour into 3 (3, 2); empty 3 (0, 2); pour (2, 0); fill 5 (2, 5); pour until the 3 ℓ jug is full, only 1 ℓ fits (3, 4): 4 ℓ in the 5 ℓ jug ✓. Six steps is the shortest way. Q4: a) 64 − 18 = 46. b) 64 + 46 = 110, minus the 5 cm overlap: 105 cm. Q5: a) breakfast: 7:25 am; after school: 4:50 pm b) 4:50 to 5:00 is 10 minutes, 25 more: 5:25 pm c) 10:45 to 11:00 is 15 minutes, 30 more minutes to 11:30: 45 minutes.

p2l9-stretch.note: Optional, if you finish early (no clock time). Open to any child who chooses it (the choice after question 3 on the worksheet). These are the SAME four questions as the printed Think harder page: the slide shows 1 to 3 and question 4 is on the page only. Never announce who is working on which page. Answers: 1) 1 apple balances 2 lemons. Swap the pomelo for 5 lemons: 2 apples and 1 lemon balance 5 lemons. Take 1 lemon off both sides: 2 apples balance 4 lemons, so 1 apple balances 2 lemons. A pomelo and an apple balance 5 + 2 = 7 lemons. 2) 1 hour 25 minutes (10:45 to 11:00 is 15 minutes, 11:00 to 12:00 is 1 hour, 12:00 to 12:10 is 10 minutes). 3) Apple 100 g, pomelo 300 g (5 apples balance 500 g). 4) (Question: You have a 2 ℓ jug and a 7 ℓ jug with no marks. How can you get exactly 3 ℓ? List each pour.) Fill 7, pour into 2, empty 2, pour again: 3 ℓ is left in the 7 ℓ jug.

p2l9-challenge.note: Optional, if you finish early (no clock time). Pairs try first, then use the "see it" slide if stuck, then the walk-through. Answers: 1) Cube 100 g, ball 200 g. 2) 10:20 am. Both are on the workbook Think Harder page (Go further 6 and 7).

p2l9-chdiag.note: Optional, if you finish early (no clock time). Show after pairs have tried, or if they are stuck. The pictures show the problem, not the answer. Ask: What do you notice on scale 1? Is there something on BOTH sides? What happens if you take it off both sides? For Q2: How many blocks are there? Which time do we know?

p2l9-chwalk.note: Optional, if you finish early (no clock time). Use after pairs have tried. Q1: the new idea is "take the same thing off both sides and it stays level". Act it out on the coat-hanger balance with two identical objects. Q2: 8:15 + 35 minutes: 8:15 to 8:45 is 30 minutes, 5 more is 8:50. Then a 10-minute break: 9:00. 9:00 + 35: 9:35. Break: 9:45. 9:45 to 10:00 is 15 minutes, 20 more: 10:20 am. Check: 3 lessons of 35 minutes and 2 breaks of 10 minutes make 125 minutes, which is 2 hours 5 minutes, and 8:15 + 2 hours 5 minutes = 10:20.

p2l9-skill1.note: Optional slide for pairs who finish early or ask for more. Show it only on request and never announce who is working on it. Children write the answer on their own paper and say it together on three; nothing is held up to the camera. Answers and tutor lines are for you only. Item 1 (Picture equations: shapes stand for numbers; tool of the day idea: Guess and check). SAY: "Find the line that tells you the most. Which shape can you find first?" ASK: "Which line did you use first and why? How can you check?" LISTEN FOR: Three triangles = 27 is the start. Then use it in line 2. ANSWER: a) 9 (27 split into 3 equal parts). b) 6 (21 - 9 = 12, shared by 2). c) 7 (13 - 6). d) 22.

p2l9-skill2.note: Optional slide for pairs who finish early or ask for more. Show it only on request and never announce who is working on it. Children write the answer on their own paper and say it together on three; nothing is held up to the camera. Answers and tutor lines are for you only. Item 1 (Calendar: weeks and days; tool of the day idea: Spot the pattern). SAY: "The week is a repeating pattern of 7. Take out whole weeks first." ASK: "How many whole weeks fit into 25 days? How many days are left over?" LISTEN FOR: "Remainder" language: 25 days is 3 weeks and 4 days. ANSWER: a) Thursday (3 weeks is 21 days, 3 full cycles). b) Monday (25 = 3 weeks and 4 days; Thursday + 4 days is Monday). c) Saturday (30 = 4 weeks and 2 days).

p2l9-talk.note: Minutes 76.5 to 81.5. Pairs talk for 90 seconds, then two volunteers share. One question: how did swapping help with the balance puzzles? Listen for: a level balance means the two sides weigh the same, so the melon can be swapped for 2 apples (or 400 g) and the scale stays level. (If a pair finishes early: a table shows how much is in each jug after every pour, so we can check every step.) Praise the reasons, not only the answers. Talk time rules: you choose volunteers first ("Who would like to share?"); never cold-call a child by name; any child may say pass; no public tallies, scores or rankings.

p2l9-exit.note: Minutes 81.5 to 86.5. No talking, no helping. Click to show the answer after the slips are in. Answer: 5:15 pm (4:50 to 5:00 is 10 minutes; 15 more minutes is 5:15). A child who writes 4:75 or 5:75 is adding minutes as if an hour had 100 minutes: plan two minutes of catch-up with the time line. Close: "You were real Measure Masters today. Next lesson is Puzzle Day!" Stamp the inquiry journal. Children keep slips on their desks and tick them against the answer on the next click; nothing is held up. About 2 minutes of child work.

p2l9-reflect.note: SPINE: Minutes 86.5 to 88.5. Start the timer (90 seconds). Say: "Pick one problem from today. Question 1: did I answer the question? Question 2: does my answer make sense? Question 3: can I check it another way? Tick, write one line, or pass. If you are still stuck, tick the box and I will come." Children tick the Look back box on the Choose and look-back page of their workbook, or just tick on paper. A pass is always allowed. It is never marked, never collected in front of the group and never read out; the tutor may look at it afterwards. If a child ticks "I am still stuck", check in during the open session next lesson (a quick visit to the shared breakout room or a hand signal, with a parent nearby; never a direct message). Do not ask children to share. Praise a check you saw, not speed. Then stamp the journals. After the look-back, minutes 88.5 to 90 are flex time (the buffer): finish stamps, then goodbye. Do not start anything new.
